operators.customDisplayName: Load Zillow ZHVI time-series table by globbing for data/wildfire/input/ZHVI.csv (fallback globs: data/wildfire/input/zhvi*.csv, data/wildfire/input/ZHVI*.csv, data/wildfire/input/*ZHVI*.csv) and reading the first match via pd.read_csv (comma delimiter, header=0, UTF-8).
Load state_abbreviation_to_state.json; convert JSON dict mapping state abbreviation -> state full name into a 2-column DataFrame [state_abbr, state_full]
Load noaa_wildfires.csv via pd.read_csv with default parameters (comma delimiter, header row=0, UTF-8)
Load noaa_wildfires_variabledescrip.csv with pd.read_csv using encoding='cp1252' (to handle smart-quote bytes like 0x92) to inspect NOAA wildfire column definitions.

Inspect ZHVI table schema: report row/column counts; list first 25 column names; detect id/geography-like columns via regex (state/region/name/county/metro/city/zip/fips/id/abbr/code); detect time-series columns matching YYYY or YYYY-MM(/DD) patterns; list columns starting with 2005 and 2010; provide a 1-row sample snapshot for up to 3 id-like columns plus one 2005 and one 2010 column when present.

Diagnostic raw preview of data/wildfire/input/ZHVI.csv using pd.read_csv(header=None, dtype=str, nrows=30) to locate the true header row / delimiter issues (does not drop any rows; for inspection only).

Compute top 3 states by total residential property value loss between 2005 and 2010 (inclusive) using ZHVI table: (1) identify state column (prefer exact names like state/state_abbr/RegionName else regex 'state'); (2) detect time-series columns formatted as YYYY, YYYY-MM, or YYYY-MM-DD; (3) select earliest column in year 2005 and latest column in year 2010; (4) coerce the two endpoint columns to numeric with errors='coerce' (preserve rows, NaN where non-numeric) and compute per-row loss = value_2005 - value_2010; (5) aggregate total_loss by state_key using sum(min_count=1) to avoid converting all-NaN groups to 0; (6) filter to positive total_loss only; (7) map 2-letter state abbreviations to full names via stateMap (left join) and fall back to original state_key when no mapping; (8) output top 3 states with [state_full, total_loss] plus the chosen endpoint column names.
